experiments.description: ACES calibration samples: periodic diamond unit cells, t/a [0.20, 0.24, 0.28], Re [1.0, 3.0, 60.0], Air at 320 K, 96 voxels per cell. Campaign 3: firm up diamond Nu (D30 scatter 0.143 sits just under the 0.15 refusal line) by adding low-Re anchors and an intermediate Re point at the thick walls where campaign 2 only had Re 10/30/100. All Re kept under the Mach ceiling observed in 02r (Re 100, wr 0.28 -> Mach 0.151).
experiments.hypothesis: Diamond Nu scatter at thick wall ratios (0.20-0.28) tightens below 0.12 once the Re spread is filled in; if it does not, diamond Nu at thick walls is genuinely broad and the refusal policy stays honest.

experiments.description: ACES calibration samples: periodic primitive unit cells, t/a [0.08, 0.12, 0.16], Re [5.0, 6.0], Air at 320 K, 96 voxels per cell. Campaign 3: pin the primitive Mach boundary (Mach/Re ~ 0.023 measured in campaign 2 -> Re 5 ~ Mach 0.115 safe, Re 6 ~ Mach 0.138 borderline). Cases over Mach 0.15 are expected to be honestly rejected by cfd-collect; that IS the boundary measurement.
experiments.hypothesis: Primitive Mach ceiling sits between Re 5 and Re 6.5 (Mach/Re ~ 0.023 from campaign 2); the fitted primitive factors (D30, constant 0.8694/3.9413) then hold over the full citable range Re <= ~6.

experiments.description: BISECTION: minimal Euler CUDA case at order 2 (was order 1). Tests whether the order-1 tet gimmik/kernel path is the NaN source.
experiments.hypothesis: order 2 survives where order 1 NaN-d on step 1 -> implicates order-1 tet kernels.

experiments.description: BISECTION: minimal Euler CUDA case with rk4 (was rk45) at order 1. Tests whether the rk45 controller/step path is the NaN source.
experiments.hypothesis: rk4 survives where rk45 NaN-d -> implicates rk45 embedded error path.

experiments.description: CUDA SANITY: pure Euler, no shock capturing, explicit rk45 dt 0.05, 100 steps. Simplest possible config on the CUDA backend.
experiments.hypothesis: if even this NaNs on CUDA but the mesh checks out, the CUDA backend in simlab-pyfr:0.3-avfix is broken on CMP 170HX.

experiments.description: BACKEND ISOLATION: identical AV dual-time case as pyfr-machdart-v3-m105-av but backend openmp (CPU). If CPU passes where CUDA NaN-d, the image CUDA kernel path is broken.
experiments.hypothesis: CPU backend survives; CUDA backend NaN indicates a kernel/gimmik issue on CMP 170HX.

experiments.description: AV probe: v3 at M 1.05, NS(mu=1e-8) + artificial-viscosity + dual sdirk33/rk45 local-pi + p-MG, 30 phys steps x dt 5. Sphere3d-proven recipe after entropy-filter NaN.
experiments.hypothesis: artificial-viscosity + dual time + p-multigrid survives the transonic start where explicit+entropy-filter NaN-d on step 1; wall forces settle.

experiments.description: PROBE dual-time: v3 at M 1.05, backward-euler dual + rk34 local-pi pseudo, entropy filter, 60 phys steps x 150 pseudo. Stability probe after explicit NaN.
experiments.hypothesis: dual-time pseudo marching is unconditionally stable enough for the impulsive transonic start; forces settle to steady values.

experiments.description: PROBE explicit: v3 at M 1.05, Euler order 1 entropy filter, dt 0.5, t 2000 (0.2 throughs). Stability probe after dt=10 NaN.
experiments.hypothesis: explicit rk45 at dt 0.5 survives the impulsive transonic start; forces finite and settling.

experiments.description: SMOKE: v3 Sears-Haack area-ruled at M 1.05, compressible Euler, order 1, coarse (lc 120 mm), 1.5 flow-throughs. Proves stability of the transonic case before production.
experiments.hypothesis: char-riem farfield + artificial viscosity keeps the impulsive start finite; wall forces settle to a plausible inviscid Cd (0.01-0.08).

experiments.description: MACH DART v2 (twin P300 config) wing at 4.4 g limit load. MTOW 136 kg -> 5868 N total lift, 2934 N per side as consistent nodal traction into the mid-thickness layer (z=0 plane) of outboard panels (|y| > 700) - voxel sloped-surface workaround, root moment preserved. Root carry-through band clamped. Carbon quasi-iso effective E 55 GPa. Double-wedge solid section, 4% t/c - screening model, no skin/spar breakdown.

experiments.description: Payload-zone subframe (twin side rails, 3 cross-members, deck plate, 4 corner legs, 2 end frames) with the payload modules as modelled solid blocks: 2x Hexagon H2-70-530X2154 tanks (250 kg each), 2x DGX B300 and the Skyworth chiller (both CHASSIS-MOUNTED per the build report - their bases are fixed and they carry no load into the subframe), centre module (350 kg fuel-cell stand-in). Loads are applied as downward face tractions on the top faces of the module blocks and flow through them into the deck and rails. Modules are solid-steel representations: stiffer than the real equipment, so reported stress is read on the FRAME only (module volumes excluded from the VM read-out). Supports: bottom faces of the four corner legs.
experiments.hypothesis: The subframe carries the full payload set at the off-road 2.5 g factor with frame stress below mild-steel yield (250 MPa), SF >= 1.5.

experiments.description: HALO-X skeleton v1 single-pin ultimate, REFERENCE run: float64 at 12 mm elements (~34M cells, ~103M DOF) to escape the float32 PCG roundoff floor seen on the 8 mm runs (relres stalled ~0.027, diverged on singlepin). ONLY the F3 carry-through band (x 1640-1700) is clamped; 35 kN longitudinal pull on the F4 keel strip (x 2040-2100, z -275..-235). Same load case as halo-skeleton-v1-singlepin c000 - this is the numerically trustworthy copy.
experiments.hypothesis: float64 converges well below the float32 floor; v1 pin-ultimate stress/deflection establishes the reference for the v1/v2 comparison.

experiments.description: HALO-X skeleton v2 launch_8g, REFERENCE run: float64 at 12 mm elements (~34M cells, ~103M DOF) to validate the float32 8 mm screening numbers (which capped at relres ~0.027). experiments.hypothesis: float64 reference confirms (within mesh-coarsening tolerance) the float32 screening ranking and magnitudes for the launch case.

Generative basis for the THREE complete aerospike motors (metal 3D print, DMLS/SLM). Angelino aerospike spike contours + ideal frozen-flow performance at 60 bar chamber, re=40 mm exit-radius class, over area ratios eps 15 / 25 / 40 (sea-level, mid, high-altitude optimised) at fixed 40% truncation (printable length, base-bleed aerospike).
